title: Per-event game coverage report
description: One row of data/curated/event-games.jsonl for every selected event, saying whether the corpus carries rows for it. It keeps 'the source has no games for this event' from looking like 'nobody fetched this event': `recorded` means the corpus emits at least one row for this event, a game or a series; `empty` means no rows are emitted while a recorded query to a game-bearing table (`ScoreboardGames`, `ScoreboardPlayers`, `MatchSchedule`) named this event and the source returned none; and `missing` means no recorded query named it. `empty` is a claim about the recorded queries, not about the outside world: the query text is the evidence to check by hand. `games` and `matches` are counts of emitted rows, so a reader can reconcile them against the files.

state.description: `recorded`: the corpus emits at least one row for this event, a game or a series. `empty`: a recorded query to a game-bearing table (`ScoreboardGames`, `ScoreboardPlayers`, `MatchSchedule`) named this event — its page, a stage page under it, or its display name, as an exact Cargo string literal rather than a substring or a `LIKE` pattern — and the source returned no rows; measured on World Cyber Games 2013 (`Tournament='World Cyber Games 2013'`) and IPL 5 (`ScoreboardPlayers`, `OverviewPage='IGN ProLeague Season 5'`). `missing`: no recorded query addressed this event's games.

games.description: How many rows this event contributes to games.jsonl.

matches.description: How many rows this event contributes to matches.jsonl.
